# Studies in History and Philosophy of Science

> **Last verified**: 2026-11-23
> **Maintainer**: @Zaious
> **Venue type**: Journal
> **Evidence basis**: Sourced under the written rule (SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md): deeper per-journal research by an AI model, directed by the maintainer, 2026-11-23; overall signal_quality **3/5**. Claims cite source URLs or counts; blanks are recorded with reasons. Independent spot-check on 2026-11-23: 7 supported and 1 partial of 8 sampled pairs; article counts corrected. No first-hand human reports; not human-verified.

> **Title note**: this is the main journal, ISSN 0039-3681. Until 2021 it was titled "Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part A"; the journal home page copy of 2026-10-17 says "Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics" and "Studies in History and Philosophy of Biological and Biomedical Sciences" (the former Parts B and C) "have merged with this journal as of January 2021" (https://web.archive.org/web/20261017095855/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science). Crossref and OpenAlex still list the ISSN under the old "Part A" name, and Crossref records from late 2021 onward carry the container title "Studies in History and Philosophy of Science" (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0039-3681). Parts B (1355-2198) and C (1369-8486) have 0 current DOIs in Crossref. The file name keeps the scaffold's "-part-a" slug.

### Review Cycle Time

> Two kinds of figures sit side by side below: the publisher's own figures on the journal home page copy of 2026-10-17 (no period stated) and small self-reported author samples (APA Journal Survey).

| Stage | Typical Time | Notes |
|-------|-------------|-------|
| **Time to first decision** | Publisher: 71 days from submission to first decision (https://web.archive.org/web/20261017095855/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science). Author reports under the former "Part A" title: 26 reports to the APA Journal Survey (2009-08-09 to 2022-06-02) give a mean response time of 4.5 months, median 3.5, range 0.3 to 12; 6 of them dated 2020-2022 give a median of 2.5 months (range 0.5 to 6). Under the current title: 3 reports (2023-05-25 to 2026-09-20) give 2.0, 4.5 and 11.0 months (https://apasurvey.philx.org/surveys/export_csv, rows for both titles) | Publisher figure has no stated period; survey figures are anonymous and self-reported |
| **Time to first review** | Publisher: 221 days from submission to the decision after review (home page copy of 2026-10-17) | The publisher labels it "decision after review" |
| **Time to acceptance (total)** | Publisher: 440 days from submission to acceptance (home page copy of 2026-10-17). Survey, "Part A" title: first verdicts of 15 revise-and-resubmit, 6 rejections, 5 conditional acceptances and 0 direct acceptances, followed by 18 acceptances at the second verdict (https://apasurvey.philx.org/surveys/export_csv) | These samples are self-selected and are not acceptance rates |
| **Time to publication (after acceptance)** | Publisher: 15 days from acceptance to online publication (home page copy of 2026-10-17). Survey: 8 "Part A" reports give 5, 1, 7, 7, 1, 1, 15 and 2.5 months from acceptance to publication | The survey figures conflict with the publisher figure and the reason was not examined |

## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double anonymized: author identities are concealed from reviewers and vice versa. All contributions are first assessed by the editor; papers judged suitable typically go to a minimum of two independent expert reviewers; the editor's decision is final (guide for authors, Wayback copy dated 2024-02-27, https://web.archive.org/web/20240227133414/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/publish/guide-for-authors). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read stating that reports are published |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank for a stated figure. Survey, "Part A" title: of 26 reports, first verdicts were 15 revise-and-resubmit, 6 rejection, 5 conditional acceptance, then 18 acceptances at the second verdict (https://apasurvey.philx.org/surveys/export_csv); average number of reviewers 2.0 (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/export_csv) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The guide's submission checklist mentions "referee suggestions and contact details" based on journal requirements; the requirement itself was not extracted |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a section "Declaration of generative AI in scientific writing" on the journal's guide for authors (Wayback copy dated 2024-02-27, link in Identity), written in line with the Elsevier AI policy for authors |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate; use is permitted only in a narrow form and with disclosure |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 (use in the writing process is limited to improving readability and language, with disclosure; stricter than the 3 given for general allow-with-disclosure rules in the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Per the 2024-02-27 guide copy: generative AI and AI-assisted tools should be used in writing only to improve readability and language, with human oversight; they cannot be authors or co-authors; authors must disclose such use in a statement placed before the references, under the heading "Declaration of Generative AI and AI-assisted technologies in the writing process"; basic grammar, spelling and reference checking tools are exempt. The guidance says it covers the writing process and not AI used to analyse data. Retrieved 2026-11-23 from the archived copy |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20240227133414/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/publish/guide-for-authors |

> Source: the journal's guide for authors (Wayback copy 2024-02-27) and the publisher's sharing page https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/sharing (retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal-specific embargo length was not found: the sharing page says embargo length varies by journal and links to a spreadsheet that was not read.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The guide says preprints can be shared anywhere at any time and that sharing a preprint on a preprint server does not count as prior publication. Because review is double anonymized, a public preprint may reveal the author |
| Under review | Blank | The guide speaks of preprints in general; it does not separately address the under-review stage |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | The accepted manuscript may be shared at once on non-commercial personal sites and privately within an institution; posting in repositories follows an embargo whose length is set per journal (spreadsheet not read). Embargo: not stated here |
| Version of Record | Open access: under the chosen licence; subscription: link sharing only | Per the sharing page: open access articles may be shared under the end-user licence selected, and public posting of a subscription-route article on social networks is not allowed |

## Format

> Source for every row unless stated: the journal's guide for authors, Wayback copy dated 2024-02-27 (https://web.archive.org/web/20240227133414/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/publish/guide-for-authors). The live guide returns HTTP 403, so current wording may differ. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The guide has one "Types of article" statement about length and names no article types. OpenAlex types 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 442 articles, 64 book reviews, 30 paratext items, 8 editorials, 4 reviews; the board page copy lists a Book Forum Editor (https://web.archive.org/web/20250128112014/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/about/editorial-board) |
| **Word limit** | Authors should aim not to exceed 12,000 words, including abstracts, footnotes and references. Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 10 pages (25th to 75th percentile 8 to 11) over 419 of 572 records that have a numeric page range, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0039-3681) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The guide words the limit as an aim; no statement on exceptions. A search-engine summary mentioned a 10,000-word figure in an older guide; it was not found in the archived copy and is not used |
| **Abstract limit** | Abstract of up to 200 words; up to 6 keywords; highlights are mandatory, 3 to 5 bullet points of at most 85 characters each, in a separate editable file |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 12,000 words. The guide says there are no strict requirements on reference formatting at submission (any consistent style); the journal's reference style, APA 7th edition, is applied to the accepted article at the proof stage |
| **Supplementary material** | The guide has sections on supplementary material and research data (sharing is encouraged); details were not extracted |
| **Figure/Table limits** | Blank. The guide has artwork and table sections; their contents were not extracted |
| **Style / submission format** | "Your Paper Your Way": a single Word or PDF file is enough at first submission, and a fully formatted editable file is requested only at revision. Double anonymized review requires a separate title page (names, affiliations, acknowledgements, declaration of interest) and an anonymized manuscript with no identifying information in text, references, figures, tables or acknowledgements. Declaration of interest required; Crossref Similarity Check may be applied |

### Orientation

> Counts: OpenAlex works of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (548 records; only 209 have an abstract, 38.1%), matching a word-boundary regex in title plus abstract; regexes are in AI-Research Notes. Shares use 209 as denominator. Abstract availability by year (records with abstract of all records): 2021 8 of 26, 2022 28 of 146, 2023 21 of 79, 2024 54 of 95, 2025 38 of 89, 2026 60 of 113, so the sample leans to recent years. A title-only cross-check over all 548 records is given where useful. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Historical and philosophical work dominates by keyword count: "histor-" 77 of 209 abstracts (36.8%), "philosoph-" 77 (36.8%), argument verbs ("I argue", "this paper argues", "I propose" and similar) 101 (48.3%), "conceptual" 25 (12.0%), against "empirical" 27 (12.9%), "case study" 26 (12.4%) and "archiv-, manuscript, correspondence or letters" 7 (3.3%) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Both are uncommon: "quantitative, statistical or regression" 16 (7.7%) and "interview, survey, questionnaire or qualitative" 10 (4.8%); these words often describe the sciences under study rather than the authors' own method |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims copy dated 2026-03-24 describes the integrated study of the history, philosophy and sociology of the sciences, including the sciences in relation to gender, culture, society and the arts, with international scope (https://web.archive.org/web/20260324151556/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/about/aims-and-scope). Subject keyword counts over 209 abstracts: biology, evolution or genetics 87 (41.6%), physics, quantum or cosmology 57 (27.3%), medicine or health 34 (16.3%), social sciences or economics 31 (14.8%), mathematics or logic 30 (14.4%), computing, data or AI 26 (12.4%), psychology or cognitive 18 (8.6%), climate or earth science 12 (5.7%), chemistry 7 (3.3%) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope statement is published by the journal: the aims copy dated 2026-03-24 describes a journal devoted to the integrated study of the history, philosophy and sociology of the sciences, encouraging the history of science, philosophy of science, historiography, and the sciences in relation to gender, culture, society and the arts (https://web.archive.org/web/20260324151556/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/about/aims-and-scope).
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with the sciences themselves: 87 of 209 abstracts match biology-related terms and 57 physics-related terms, and argument verbs appear in 101 (48.3%) (Orientation).
- **Article type and length**: aim for no more than 12,000 words including abstracts, footnotes and references; abstract up to 200 words; up to 6 keywords; highlights of 3 to 5 bullets are mandatory (guide copy dated 2024-02-27, https://web.archive.org/web/20240227133414/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/publish/guide-for-authors).
- **Journal merger**: since January 2021 the journal also takes the former Part B (modern physics) and Part C (biological and biomedical sciences) remit (home page copy dated 2026-10-17); 36 of 548 works carry primary topic "Quantum Mechanics and Applications".
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are OpenAlex works of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (548 records, 209 with abstract, 38.1%) whose title or abstract matches the regex in AI-Research Notes; shares use 209 as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method word appears, not how a reviewer would judge it; in a journal about the sciences these words often describe the sciences under study (history of experiments, philosophy of statistics) rather than the author's own method, so the scores for experiment and statistics are inflated. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | "experiment-, experimental or randomised" 22 of 209 (10.5%); "quantitative, statistical or regression" 16 (7.7%); see the inflation caveat above |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "interview, survey, questionnaire or qualitative" 10 of 209 (4.8%); "sociolog-, STS or ethnograph-" 10 (4.8%) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph-" 0 of 209 abstracts and 0 of 548 titles |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "philosoph-" 77 of 209 (36.8%); argument verbs 101 (48.3%); "conceptual" 25 (12.0%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | "mixed methods" 0 of 209 |
| Meta-analysis | 1 | "systematic review or meta-analysis" 1 of 209 (0.5%) |
| Historical / archival (added row) | 3 | "histor-" 77 of 209 (36.8%); "archiv-, manuscript, correspondence or letters" 7 (3.3%); "historiograph-" 6 (2.9%) |
| Formal modelling (added row) | 3 | "formal, model, simulation, Bayesian or mathematic-" 67 of 209 (32.1%); the word "model" is common in the philosophy of science generally |
| Case study (added row) | 3 | "case study" 26 of 209 (12.4%) |

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| **Dominant tradition** | The archived board page lists 94 persons: one editor-in-chief, 8 associate editors, one book forum editor and the remaining board members, with research-interest tags only for some (for example philosophy of biology, philosophy of physics, history of medicine, science and technology studies, quantum foundations). No discipline split can be counted because most entries carry no tag. Topic mix of published work: 206 of 548 works have OpenAlex primary topic "Philosophy of Biology and Scientific Explanation" | https://web.archive.org/web/20250128112014/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/about/editorial-board ; OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23; board composition may have changed since |

| **Review model** | Double anonymized; at least two independent expert reviewers are typical; editor screening comes first | Guide copy dated 2024-02-27 (URL in Peer Review) |

| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No source states reviewer attitudes; qualitative interview or survey words appear in 10 of 209 abstracts, which does not show how reviewers treat such work | Methodological Preferences counts |
| **Discourse community signals (author side and editorial board)** | Board persons by recount: 40 of 94 in the United States, 17 in the United Kingdom, 7 in Canada, 6 in the Netherlands. Authors: 119 of 442 articles have a US-based author, 66 a German-based author, 60 a UK-based author (OpenAlex) | Board page above and OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The guide copy (2024-02-27) expects authors to follow institutional and national guidelines on informed consent from living subjects, and adds that authors not affiliated with an institution should consult the editors at submission (https://web.archive.org/web/20240227133414/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science/publish/guide-for-authors). It states no journal-specific ethics-approval procedure |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers dominate: 327 of 442 articles (74.0%) dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex authorships) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The guide copy tells authors without an institutional affiliation to consult the editors at submission (URL above) and asks for affiliations on the title page; no further independent-scholar rule is stated |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The guide copy encourages sharing of supporting data and offers ways to link or state data availability; a mandate was not found in the text read |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double anonymized review: separate title page and an anonymized manuscript with no identifying information in text, references, figures, tables or acknowledgements (guide copy dated 2024-02-27). Preprints are allowed anywhere at any time, which may reveal the author (https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/sharing) |
| **AI use** | Disclosure statement required for generative AI in writing, and use is limited to readability and language (guide copy dated 2024-02-27) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC USD 3,830 excluding taxes if open access is chosen, and no publication fee on the subscription route (home page copy dated 2026-10-17, https://web.archive.org/web/20261017095855/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/studies-in-history-and-philosophy-of-science); 213 of 442 recent articles are hybrid open access in OpenAlex |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 3 (only 209 of 548 records have abstracts, 38.1%, skewed to 2024-2026, so keyword counts are lower bounds with a recent-year tilt; regexes are word-bounded and listed below); journal-specific policies and guidelines 3 (Wayback copies of the journal's own pages dated 2024-02-27 to 2026-10-17; live pages unreadable); publisher-wide policies 3 (sharing page read, embargo spreadsheet not); experiential layer 2 (APA Journal Survey: 26 reports under the old title and 3 under the new one, self-reported and anonymous; SciRev has no reviews).

**Method note:** OpenAlex works were fetched with page-based paging (no key, no email, one request per 2 seconds; no HTTP 429 occurred). Counts are computed locally over title plus reconstructed abstract with the regexes below (case-insensitive unless a name is marked case-sensitive); word-boundary matching avoids substring inflation. Crossref lists 572 journal-article records for the window but none carries an abstract, so Crossref was used only for record counts and page ranges. The scoring convention is stated in Methodological Preferences.

**Regexes used** (all with word boundaries): history `histor\w+`; archive `archiv\w+|manuscripts?|correspondence|letters?`; philosophy `philosoph\w+`; sociology/STS `sociolog\w+|STS|science and technology studies|ethnograph\w+`; case study `case stud(y|ies)`; conceptual `conceptual`; argue `I argue|we argue|this (paper|article|essay) argues?|I (defend|propose|suggest|claim|show|offer)|we (defend|propose|suggest|claim|show|offer)`; empirical `empirical\w*`; experiment `experiments?|experimental|randomi[sz]ed`; interview/survey/qualitative `interviews?|surveys?|questionnaires?|qualitative`; quantitative `quantitative|statistic\w*|regression`; formal/model `formal\w*|model(l)?ing|models?|simulation\w*|Bayesian|mathematic\w+`; review `systematic review|meta-analys\w+`; mixed `mixed[- ]methods?`; autoethnography `autoethnograph\w*`; historiography `historiograph\w+`; named figures case-sensitive (for example `Kuhn\w*`, `Newton\w*`, `Darwin\w*`); realism `realis\w+`; antirealism `constructive empiricism|anti-?realis\w+|instrumentalis\w+`; pragmatism `pragmati\w+`; feminist `feminis\w+`; physics `physic\w+|quantum|relativity|cosmolog\w+|thermodynamic\w*|particle`; biology `biolog\w+|evolution\w*|gene\w*|ecolog\w+|Darwin\w*|species`; medicine `medic\w+|health|clinical|disease\w*|epidemiolog\w+|psychiatr\w+`; mathematics `mathematic\w+|logic\w*|proof\w*`; chemistry `chemi\w+`; psychology `psycholog\w+|cognitive|neuro\w+`; social science `social science\w*|economic\w*|sociolog\w+|anthropolog\w+`; climate/earth `climate|geolog\w+|earth science\w*`; computing `comput\w+|machine learning|artificial intelligence|AI|big data|algorithm\w*|data`; gender `gender\w*|feminis\w+|women|sexis\w+`; race `rac(e|ial|ism|ist)|whiteness|slavery|eugenic\w*`; decolonial `decoloni\w+|indigenous|postcolonial\w*|colonial\w*|imperial\w*`; queer `queer|trans(gender)?|LGBT\w*|sexual orientation|homosexual\w*`; religion `religio\w+|Christian\w*|Islam\w*|Buddhis\w+|theolog\w+|Jewish|Judais\w+`; war `Nazi\w*|war|Cold War|military|weapon\w*|nuclear`; COVID `COVID\w*|pandemic`; AI `artificial intelligence|AI|ChatGPT|machine learning|large language model\w*|LLMs?`; politics/values `political|politics|democra\w+|values?|ethic\w*|policy`; climate/environment `climate|environment\w*|Anthropocene`; ## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the aims copy describes a journal for the history, philosophy and sociology of the sciences (Framing Requirements); a paper with no engagement with the sciences is outside the stated scope.
- **Anonymisation**: review is double anonymized and the manuscript must carry no identifying information, with a separate title page (Format; Practical Concerns).
- **Front matter**: abstract up to 200 words, up to 6 keywords and mandatory highlights of 3 to 5 bullets (Format; archived guide of 2024-02-27).
- **AI use**: generative AI may be used in writing only to improve readability and language, with a disclosure statement (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; the 12,000-word figure is worded as an aim (Format), and the guide is a 2024 copy.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher figures are 71 days to first decision, 221 days to decision after review and 440 days to acceptance (Review Cycle Time), which is long; the author survey for the former "Part A" title gives a median of 3.5 months to a response (26 reports).
- **Cost**: open access carries an APC of USD 3,830 excluding taxes; the subscription route has no publication fee (Open Access).
- **Anonymisation work**: a separate title page and an anonymized manuscript, and a public preprint may reveal the author (Format; Preprint Policy).
- **Style**: no strict reference formatting is required at submission (any consistent style); APA 7th edition is the journal's style and is applied at the proof stage, so reformatting to APA before submission is not required by the guide (Format; guide copy 2024-02-27).

### Best Suited For

- Historical and philosophical studies of particular sciences, especially biology and physics: 87 and 57 of 209 abstracts, and 206 of 548 works carry primary topic "Philosophy of Biology and Scientific Explanation" (Orientation; Subject Density).
- Work that combines history with philosophy: "histor-" and "philosoph-" each appear in 77 of 209 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Argument-led papers on science, values and policy: 51 of 209 abstracts match politics, values or policy terms (Sensitive Topics).
- Single-author work: 327 of 442 articles (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Primarily empirical or interview-based social-science studies: "interview, survey, questionnaire or qualitative" appears in 10 of 209 abstracts (Methodological Preferences). The count shows the form is rare here, not that it is rejected.
- Work with no connection to the sciences (Hard Blockers).
- Anyone who needs a fast, verified turnaround: the publisher's own figures are 221 days to a decision after review and 440 days to acceptance (Review Cycle Time).
- Papers needing a stated acceptance rate or desk-rejection data before choosing: none exists in the sources read (Metrics).
